title: Version-drift detection + refresh process (containers/tools/DBs)
context: Containers and tools pinned by immutable digest guarantee reproducibility of past reanalyses, but over time upstream images and reference databases (UniProt releases, contaminant databases) change. Without a drift detection process, the project would not know when a pinned environment has become stale or when a security patch in a base image matters. Drift does not invalidate past results but creates maintenance tasks: new reanalyses should use up-to-date references, and stale pipelines become explicit maintenance items.
objective: Implement a version-drift detection process that regularly checks for upstream changes (new container image versions, tool releases, reference-DB updates) and converts detected drift into tracked maintenance tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: A drift detection script or CI workflow is implemented that checks for: new versions of pinned analysis tools (MaxQuant/FragPipe/DIA-NN etc.), updates to base container images, and new releases of reference databases (UniProt).
Detected drift is surfaced as a GitHub issue or tracked maintenance task — not silently ignored.
The process documents how to refresh a pinned pipeline: update digests, update the run manifest schema references, and re-run CI smoke test.
The drift detection code is committed as a PR with MIT license; pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; commit is DCO signed-off.
output: A committed PR containing a version-drift detection script/workflow and a documented refresh process; MIT-licensed.
